question.text:
Statement I Boron always forms covalent bond
Statement II The small size of $\mathrm{B}^{3+}$ favours formation of covalent bond.

options.text: Statement I is true, Statement II is true, Statement II is a correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is true, Statement II is true, Statement II is not a correct explanation for Statement II
Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true

solution.text: Boron always form covalent bond because boron requires very high energy to form $\mathrm{B}^{3+}$ and again $\mathrm{B}^{3+}$ due to its very small size having high polarising power thus cause greater polarisation and eventually significant covalent characteristics-Fajans rule.
